children: The Czech central bank (CNB) left its main repo rate (CZCBIR=ECI) unchanged at 3.75% as expected on Thursday, extending last month's pause after hiking for the first time in four years in June.
The bank has pointed out inflation risks but also that it is in a comfortable position with rates standing well above inflation which reached 1.9% in August, below the bank's target of 2%.
A Reuters poll last week showed all 11 analysts believed that the bank would keep the repo rate steady, and only two out of eight forecast a 25 basis-point hike in the rest of the year.

However, the bank has seen risks on the upside. Price growth led by consumption and investments, as well as growing government spending, has been offset mainly by falling food prices, which central bankers and analysts expect to reverse course in the coming months.
Rising wages and lending, the global energy price shock, and government plans to increase the budget deficit next year to around 3.5% of GDP, also point in an inflationary direction.

Another one-off inflation factor will be the base effect of energy subsidies which took about 0.4 percentage points off inflation this year, and will drop out of the comparative base in January, causing a reverse effect. That is expected to put inflation above 3% in early 2027.
The bank will next meet on policy in November, when it will also discuss a quarterly update to its economic forecasts.
The interest rate market has been rising across the curve, with short term interest rates pricing in as many as four interest rate hikes in the coming year.
Central bank Vice-Governor Eva Zamrazilova and board member Jan Kubicek have said that the market was reflecting considerations beyond monetary policy in the pricing.
Central bank Governor Ales Michl was due to present the board decision at a news conference at 3 p.m. (1300 GMT).
